summary: Bhikkhu Pāsādika is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned an MA from Magadh University (~1961–1964) and a PhD from Punjabi University (~1970–1974), later holding positions at Punjabi University, Marburg, Bochum, Würzburg, and the Frankfurt Buddhist Academy.

Bhikkhu U Dhammissara is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he studied under MA supervisor Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007) under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe, having also studied under Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and N. A. Jayawickrama.

Bhogilal Sandesara (1917–1995) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh. He served as Head of the Gujarati Department at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda from circa 1951 to 1975.
Bhuvan Chandel is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She served as Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1999–2004) and held a professorship at Panjab University (attested 2003).

Bhuwan Lal Joshi (1930–1977) was an Indology scholar who studied at Patna University. He held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1962–1967) and served as a professor at the University of California, Santa Cruz (~1970–1977).

Bidia Dandaron (1914–1974) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg institutions, including under Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov, and with traditional teacher Lubsan Sandan Tsydenov. He was a research fellow at the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies.

Bimal Krishna Matilal (1935–1991) worked in philosophy and Indology. Educated at University of Calcutta and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, he taught at University of Toronto (~1968–1977) before serving as Oxford's Spalding Professor of Eastern Religion and Ethics (1977–1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha (1919–2002) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned degrees from Patna University and the University of London under Lionel David Barnett, later serving as head of department at Patna University and at Patna College.

Bing Chen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Sichuan University from circa 1987 to 2015 and held a post at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences (attested 1993).
Bingtao Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from Peking University in 2008 and completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xueyu (attested 2015).

Birgit Kellner is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She received her doctorate from Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura and has held posts at the University of Vienna and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Bisheshwar Nath Reu (1890–1966) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. He headed the Archaeological Survey of India, Government Museum Jodhpur (~1927–1950), Sumer Public Library (~1923–1950), and Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre.
Biswanath Banerjee (1926–2018) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University (1967–1991) and served as president of The Asiatic Society (~2003–2007).
Bo Jiang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2008).

Bo Utas is an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Uppsala University (~1957–1973) under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Stig Wikander, and later held an academic post at Uppsala University (~1988–2003).
Bo-Kwang Han is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2004 and 2015).
Bokar Rinpoche (1940–2004) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1965–1989). He held a post at Bokar Monastery from circa 1984 until 2004.

Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD at Princeton University under the doctoral supervision of Stephen F. Teiser.

Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and served as a professor of philosophy at Florida International University (1991–1992, attested 2012).
